headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0216 — This PDF job was too big for SMTO to handle at once

html:
SMTO-EXE-0216 — This PDF job was too big for SMTO to handle at once

GUID: a3a69231-cdd9-5e2c-8ae7-1dd6be945ab5
Slug: pdf-resource-limit-exceeded
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • The PDF work needed more pages, memory or time than SMTO allows in one go, or the Gateway was already busy with other PDF jobs. Your original PDF was not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to work on fewer pages at a time, for example 10 pages per request. Each request has limits on pages, memory and time, and smaller requests stay within them.
  2. For page images or text reading, ask for a lower quality such as 144 DPI. Higher quality makes much larger images that take more memory and time.
  3. If other PDF tasks are running at the same time, wait for them to finish, then ask again. Each Gateway computer works on at most four PDF jobs at once.
  4. If you asked for a new file, check Artifacts from this run before asking again. This avoids making duplicate files if part of the work was already saved.

What success looks like

  • The smaller request completes and its result or new file appears under Artifacts from this run.

If it still fails

  • If even a single page fails, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, since the Gateway's PDF helper may be crashing. Don't edit the original PDF to make it fit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • PDF processing on the Gateway exceeded a resource limit (parser stream/tree/form size, result size, memory, time, or four concurrent PDF jobs), or the isolated PDF worker exited unsuccessfully.

What this means

  • PDF processing exceeded parser/stream/tree/form/result bounds, active-worker capacity or memory/recursion limits; an unsuccessful isolated worker exit also maps here without identifying one limit. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • PDF processing exceeded parser/stream/tree/form/result bounds, active-worker capacity or memory/recursion limits; an unsuccessful isolated worker exit also maps here without identifying one limit.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify file structure, selected pages/DPI, output size or concurrency evidence before assuming the entire source is too large.

How to fix it

  • Reduce scope: at most 100 selected pages (10 for render/OCR), DPI 72-300 with a 20-megapixel page limit, a 60-second worker budget, 1 GiB worker memory, a 2 MB result envelope and four active PDF jobs per Gateway. An unexplained non-zero worker exit also lands here, so inspect the Gateway for crashes before altering the document; check the run's artifacts before repeating a write.
  • Reduce the specific bounded work or let active operations settle when appropriate; inspect an unexplained worker failure before changing the document.

Retry and execution caution

  • Select fewer pages or lower DPI, or use a smaller document. The isolated worker exceeded its resource budget.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported scoped work completes within its applicable bounds with all required output retained.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
